newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament speaker to boycott Chirac visit.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament speaker to boycott Chirac visit.

text.p: Israel's parliament speaker said on Saturday he would boycott a visit to the Jewish state next week by French President Jacques Chirac because it did not include a stop in parliament.
Chirac was due on Monday in Israel, the second destination in his six-day Middle East tour aimed at increasing European influence over peace moves in the region.

"The Knesset (parliament) symbolises the democracy in Israel...and it is only right that such a leader visit the Knesset and I don't know why he decided to cancel his visit to the Knesset," speaker Dan Tichon told Israel's army radio.
Asked if he would boycott Chirac's visit, Tichon said: "Yes, certainly."
"This is a symbolic act, a positive one in my opinion and I'm sure that when they hear about the steps I intend to take they will surely think again and maybe a solution will be found," he said.
Tichon pointed out that while Chirac cancelled his visit to the Knesset, he was planning to attend a session of the Palestinian National Council.
Chirac is expected to urge Israel to resume peace talks with Syria and implement its agreements with the Palestinians.
Arab leaders have welcomed European involvement in the U.S.-mediated peace talks but Israel has been reluctant to give the Europeans any official role.
Chirac arrived in Syria on Saturday at the start of his tour which also takes him to Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt.
